newsitem.title: FRANCE: Son of Israel's Herzog granted bail in France.
newsitem.headline: Son of Israel's Herzog granted bail in France.

text.p: The son of former Israeli president Chaim Herzog was released on bail on Friday from a southern French prison where he had been held since December in a probe into his alleged role in a casino sleaze scandal.

Joel Herzog, 47, is suspected of complicity in the payment of a 1.45 million franc ($250,000) bribe to Michel Mouillot, former mayor of the French Riviera resort city of Cannes, who is also in detention.
Herzog was released on 300,000 francs ($52,000) bail.
"I am delighted to see my family and my children," he told reporters as he left prison in the town of Grasse.

The case involves a requested municipal permit to install 100 extra slot machines in the Grand Riviera Casino in the Noga-Hilton Hotel which belongs to Herzog's father-in-law, Swiss businessman Nissim Gaon, who is also under investigation.
Herzog, who holds dual British and Israeli citizenship, usually lives in Switzerland where he works as an administrator in Gaon's business empire.
